sections.h2: Where is Huntington, WV, and how is the city laid out?
sections.html:
Huntington sits on the southern bank of the Ohio River where the Guyandotte River joins it, in the southwestern corner of West Virginia. It is the county seat of Cabell County, and small parts of the city extend into Wayne County. Wikipedia reports a 2020 census population of 46,842, an estimate of 44,942 for 2024, and a ranking as the second-largest city in the state.

The city covers about 18.5 square miles, of which roughly 16.2 are land, and sits at 564 feet above sea level. Streets follow a grid. Avenues run east and west alongside the river, with Third and Fifth Avenues as the wide boulevards, and numbered streets run north and south.

Locals divide the city into four sections. The CSX railroad tracks split north from south, and First Street splits east from west. Within those sections you find:

  • Downtown and the Marshall University campus
  • West Huntington, Old Central City and Westmoreland on the west side
  • Ritter Park, South Side, Enslow Park and the Southeast Hills to the south
  • Walnut Hills, Guyandotte, Highlawn and Forest Hills on the east side

Knowing which section your house sits in helps when you talk to any buyer.

sections.h2: What shaped Huntington's economy and housing stock?
sections.html:
Huntington grew as a rail, river and steel town, and the housing stock still reflects that. According to Wikipedia, the city was founded in 1871 by Collis P. Huntington, and its boom years ran until the Great Flood of 1937.

Population peaked decades ago and has fallen in every census since 1950. The city went from 86,353 residents in 1950 to 46,842 in 2020.

The job base has shifted toward health care and education. Wikipedia lists the largest employers as Marshall University, Cabell Huntington Hospital, St. Mary's Medical Center, Amazon, DirecTV and the City of Huntington. St. Mary's alone is described as the largest private employer in Cabell County, with more than 2,600 employees.

Jobs like these bring relocations in and out, and some of those owners need a quick closing.

sections.h2: How do floods and weather affect a Huntington house sale?
sections.html:
The Ohio River is the reason Huntington has flood walls, and flood history is part of the city's story. The Great Flood of 1937 killed five people, left tens of thousands homeless and led to the construction of the flood walls in 1938, according to Wikipedia. Buyers and lenders still ask about flood zone status, so check your address on the state's flood map tool before you list.

The climate is humid subtropical at the northern edge of its range. Snowfall averages about 19.8 inches a season, and a typical year brings 24 afternoons at or above 90 degrees.

None of this makes a house unsellable, but roof, basement and heating condition are what any buyer will price in.

sections.h2: What local rules does a Huntington seller or landlord need to know?
sections.html:
The biggest local rule for owners with tenants is the rental registry and inspection program. Huntington City Council adopted an ordinance in 2018 requiring rental units to meet building, fire, health, safety and zoning codes. The city's rental inspection page explains how it works.

The city cites a 2020 housing report that found 6,050 of its 9,603 rental units, or 63 percent, in decline, and estimated that 60 to 80 percent did not meet code.

  • One and two family rentals are inspected no more than once in 12 months per unit.
  • Inspections cover electrical safety, heating, smoke alarms, handrails and general maintenance.
  • Tenants can request an inspection without the landlord's permission.
  • Apartment buildings with more than two units go through the building, electrical and plumbing inspectors and the fire marshal.

If you own a rental you want to sell, an open violation or an unregistered unit can slow a conventional buyer's lender. A buyer paying cash can often take the property with those issues still open. For code complaints on vacant or neglected property, the city directory lists the Public Works office at 304-696-4414.

The 2023 registry packet listed a $75 inspection fee and a $20 business license, so confirm current fees with the city before relying on those figures.

sections.h2: How does property tax work for a house in Huntington?
sections.html:
Huntington homes are taxed by Cabell County, with the Cabell County Assessor valuing the property and the Sheriff's Tax Office collecting the bill. The assessor's FAQ page lists the 2026 levy rates for owner occupied homes as 1.6752 inside the City of Huntington and 1.3552 in the rural part of the county. Residents of the cities of Barboursville and Milton pay their own city rates.

West Virginia sorts property into classes. Class 2 is owner occupied residential property, and Classes 3 and 4 cover non owner occupied property. A house that stops being your primary residence, for example after you move out and rent it or leave it empty, is assessed differently, which is a common surprise for heirs.

Under the state due dates, bills go out on or after July 15, the first half is due September 1 and the second half March 1. A 2.5 percent discount applies if you pay before those dates. Unpaid first half taxes become delinquent October 1 and second half taxes April 1, and delinquent taxes accrue interest at 9 percent a year.

In Cabell County, owners aged 65 or older who have lived in West Virginia for two consecutive years can apply for the homestead exemption between July 1 and December 1. The state describes the benefit as an exemption of the first $20,000 of assessed value.

sections.h2: What does it cost to transfer a house in West Virginia?
sections.html:
West Virginia charges an excise tax on the privilege of transferring real estate, and it is the main closing tax on a deed. Under section 11-22-2 of the state code the rate is $1.10 for each $500 of value, and the county collects it. A second county excise tax of 55 cents per $500 also applies, and a county commission may raise that to a maximum of $1.65 per $500 by vote.

The grantor, meaning the seller, pays unless the buyer accepts the deed without the tax being paid. The clerk also collects a $20 fee that goes to the state Affordable Housing Fund when real estate is transferred for consideration.

Sale price$1.10 per $500Add 55 cents per $500
$60,000$132$198
$100,000$220$330
$150,000$330$495

These examples are arithmetic from the statute rates, not a quote, and your county's actual combined rate may differ. Deeds in Cabell County are recorded with the County Clerk, whose records include a deed lookup. Transfers by will or through a list of heirs are excluded from the tax under section 11-22-1, which matters for inherited homes.

sections.h2: Which Huntington sellers usually consider a cash sale?
sections.html:
Sellers in Huntington who consider a cash sale usually face one of a few situations, and each one has a local twist. The common thread is a house that would take time and money to prepare for a conventional listing.

  • Heirs holding an older home in Old Central City, Guyandotte or the South Side that no one wants to maintain.
  • Landlords with units that fail the city's rental inspection and need work they cannot fund.
  • Owners relocating for a job at one of the hospitals or Marshall University on a short timeline.
  • Homes with a damp basement, an aging roof or an outdated furnace that would draw repair demands from a buyer's inspector.

A cash offer skips the lender's appraisal and the repair negotiation after inspection. Cash Home Buyers reviews each Huntington property individually, and an offer depends on the condition, location and the work the house needs. If the numbers do not suit you, you can say no and owe nothing.

Before you accept any offer, ask for the closing to be handled by a West Virginia title company or attorney, confirm who pays the transfer tax, and get the payoff on any mortgage or tax lien in writing.

sections.h2: How do Huntington's roads and transit affect where a house sells?
sections.html:
Interstate 64 and US 60 shape how buyers think about Huntington. Exits 6 through 15 of I-64 serve the city, and US 52 connects at exit 6. US 60, part of the historic Midland Trail, runs along the river through downtown and splits into Third and Fifth Avenues.

The Huntington and Ashland metro area spans seven counties in three states, with an estimated 368,000 residents, so buyers and renters often come from across the river.

The assessor's page also links to the Tri-State Transit Authority and the Greater Huntington Park and Recreation District, handy references when you describe the area to an out of town buyer.

faqs.q: How fast can I sell my house in Huntington, WV?
faqs.a: A cash sale can close faster than a conventional sale because there is no lender appraisal. The exact timing depends on title work and the Cabell County Clerk's recording process. Ask for a closing date in writing before you sign.

faqs.q: Do I pay a transfer tax when I sell in Huntington?
faqs.a: Yes, in most sales. West Virginia charges $1.10 per $500 of value, plus a county excise tax that starts at 55 cents per $500, and the seller normally pays. Inherited transfers by will or list of heirs are excluded under section 11-22-1.

faqs.q: What happens to my Huntington rental if it fails an inspection?
faqs.a: The city requires a landlord to correct violations found at a registered rental inspection. If you sell instead, a cash buyer can take the property as is, but disclose known problems and confirm the sale with your title company.

faqs.q: When are Cabell County property taxes due?
faqs.a: The first half is due September 1 and the second half March 1. First half taxes become delinquent October 1, and second half taxes April 1. A 2.5 percent discount applies when you pay early.

faqs.q: Can I sell a house in Huntington that I inherited?
faqs.a: Yes, once you have legal authority to convey the title. That usually means the estate has been opened with the county. A title company can tell you which documents the deed needs.
